artifact.recommendation: Use field-specific merge rules with monotonic account-status precedence and version metadata.
reasoning: This preserves multi-region write availability during partitions while allowing ordinary profile conflicts to converge automatically.
Account status should merge so suspended dominates active; only a distinct, explicit reviewed-unsuspend operation may restore active status.
Wall-clock last-write-wins is unsafe because observed clock skew can cause stale active data to override a suspension.
Existing unique operation IDs can support idempotency, deduplication, and deterministic reconciliation.
considerations: Define deterministic per-field rules for concurrent profile edits, using causal or logical version metadata and a stable tie-breaker when necessary.
Represent reviewed unsuspend as a distinct authorized operation rather than an ordinary status assignment.
Retain reconciliation audit records, including operation IDs, versions, merge decisions, and authorization context.
Test convergence under duplicate delivery, reordering, retries, and partitions lasting at least one hour.
assumptions: The defined status precedence and reviewed-unsuspend distinction are enforced in both online writes and asynchronous reconciliation.
Version metadata can be introduced without violating current storage or replication constraints.
Profile fields do not independently carry authorization consequences comparable to account status.
risks: An incorrect or inconsistent implementation of status precedence across regions could permit authorization regression.
A simple permanent suspended-dominates-active rule could block legitimate unsuspension unless reviewed-unsuspend semantics causally supersede the relevant suspension.
Concurrent reviewed-unsuspend and new-suspension operations require an explicit rule; safety should favor the new suspension unless ordering proves the unsuspend reviewed that suspension.
Unbounded version metadata or operation-history retention could create storage and maintenance overhead.
evidence_needed: Detailed status state-machine semantics, especially concurrency between reviewed unsuspension and later suspension.
Selection and compatibility assessment of version metadata, such as hybrid logical clocks, Lamport versions, or version vectors.
Per-profile-field conflict policy and confirmation that no profile field affects authorization.
Cross-region reconciliation tests proving deterministic convergence and stale-data safety.

Suspended must dominate active until an explicit reviewed unsuspend action.
Both regions already provide unique operation IDs suitable for reconciliation and deduplication.
Both regions must remain writable for profile updates during partitions up to one hour.
The resolver can distinguish reviewed unsuspend operations from ordinary updates.
Profile conflicts are rare, supporting automatic deterministic reconciliation.

artifact.recommendation: Use field-specific merge rules with monotonic account-status precedence and version metadata. Merge ordinary profile fields automatically using deterministic per-field rules; make suspended dominate active unless a distinct, explicit reviewed-unsuspend operation causally supersedes the suspension. Retain unique operation IDs for deduplication and auditability.
reasoning: Last-write-wins based on wall-clock timestamps is unsafe because observed regional clock skew can misorder operations, potentially allowing stale active status to override suspended.
Monotonic status precedence directly satisfies the authorization invariant while the explicit reviewed-unsuspend operation provides a controlled path back to active.
Field-specific merging allows rare profile conflicts to converge automatically without unnecessarily applying the stricter status policy to non-security-sensitive fields.
Keeping both regions writable during partitions satisfies the stated business-continuity requirement; disabling regional writes does not.
Existing unique operation IDs and conflict-resolution support for reviewed unsuspends reduce implementation complexity and enable idempotent reconciliation.
considerations: Define deterministic merge behavior for every profile field, including tie-breaking for concurrent operations, deletions, and null values.
Use causal or logical version metadata—such as version vectors or hybrid logical clocks—for ordering and concurrency detection; do not rely solely on wall-clock time.
Model reviewed unsuspend as a distinct authenticated operation referencing or causally succeeding the relevant suspension, rather than as an ordinary active-value write.
Persist conflict and status-transition audit records, and make reconciliation idempotent through operation IDs.
Test convergence under duplicated, reordered, delayed, and concurrently delivered operations across partitions of at least one hour.
assumptions: The defined status precedence is authoritative and suspended should dominate all ordinary active writes regardless of timestamp.
A reviewed unsuspend can be securely authenticated and represented distinctly in the replicated operation stream.
Version metadata can be added without violating storage, latency, or compatibility constraints.
The requirement to remain writable applies to profile updates and does not require unrestricted ordinary status changes during partitions.
risks: An incorrectly specified reviewed-unsuspend rule could reactivate an account despite a concurrent or later suspension.
Incomplete per-field merge definitions could cause replicas to diverge or silently discard legitimate profile updates.
Version-vector metadata may grow with the number of writers unless bounded to regions or otherwise compacted.
Legacy records or consumers that do not understand the new metadata and operation types could apply unsafe fallback behavior.
A monotonic rule without lifecycle handling may leave accounts suspended indefinitely when causal history is unavailable or corrupted.
evidence_needed: A complete account-status state machine, including concurrent suspend and reviewed-unsuspend semantics.
The number and identity model of independent writers needed to select and size the version-metadata scheme.
Per-profile-field business rules and whether any profile fields also influence authorization.
Retention, audit, and rollback requirements for reconciliation operations.
Compatibility and migration behavior for existing records, APIs, caches, and downstream consumers.

citations.claim: Regional clock skew has reached 47 seconds, making wall-clock last-write-wins unsafe for authorization-sensitive status.
Suspended must dominate active until an explicit reviewed unsuspend action.
Both regions already attach unique operation IDs to writes.
Both regions must continue accepting profile updates during partitions lasting up to one hour.
Conflict-resolution code can distinguish reviewed unsuspend operations from ordinary profile updates.
Profile conflicts are rare, supporting automatic deterministic reconciliation rather than sacrificing availability.

strengths: The recommendation directly matches the option that satisfies all three stated constraints: partition-time writability, automatic profile convergence, and protection against stale reactivation.
It correctly rejects wall-clock last-write-wins using the documented 47-second regional clock skew and explains the authorization consequence.
It separates security-sensitive account status reconciliation from ordinary profile-field reconciliation instead of applying one unsafe policy universally.
It correctly incorporates explicit reviewed-unsuspend operations as the controlled exception to suspended-over-active precedence.
It makes practical use of existing unique operation IDs for deduplication, idempotency, and auditability.
The considerations cover important implementation details, including deterministic tie-breaking, nulls, deletions, causal metadata, replay behavior, and adverse-delivery testing.
The report clearly identifies migration, metadata growth, incomplete merge rules, and concurrent suspension/unsuspension as material risks.
Its citations accurately map the central claims to the supplied evidence.
weaknesses: The recommendation leaves the exact causal semantics of reviewed unsuspension unresolved, particularly how it interacts with concurrent or later suspensions.
It suggests version vectors or hybrid logical clocks without selecting a metadata model or explaining whether each can enforce the required status semantics.
The phrase 'causally supersedes the suspension' is underspecified when histories are incomplete, operations are concurrent, or multiple suspensions exist.
The profile strategy is described only as deterministic per-field rules; no example rules or criteria are supplied for choosing among multi-value retention, precedence, or explicit user resolution.
The report does not distinguish clearly between operation deduplication and conflict ordering; unique operation IDs solve the former but not the latter.
The confidence value of 0.98 is too high given the acknowledged absence of the complete status state machine, writer topology, field classifications, and migration constraints.
unsupported: The claim that existing operation IDs and reviewed-unsuspend detection reduce implementation complexity is plausible but not directly established by the evidence; integration and migration complexity remain unknown.
Auditability is not guaranteed merely by retaining unique operation IDs; it also requires durable operation history, actor identity, timestamps or logical ordering, and retention controls.
The proposal assumes causal or logical metadata can be introduced across all replicas and consumers, but feasibility is not supported by the provided evidence.
Testing partitions of 'at least one hour' is reasonable but does not establish sufficient coverage of longer outages, recovery backlogs, or metadata compaction behavior.
missing: A precise account-status state machine defining suspend, reviewed unsuspend, repeated suspension, concurrent transitions, and precedence across all status values.
An explicit invariant such as: an account may become active only when a valid reviewed-unsuspend operation observes and clears every suspension relevant under the chosen causal model.
A decision on whether status-changing operations are permitted in both regions during partitions and, if so, which operations are accepted locally.
Identification of every profile field that affects authentication, authorization, risk, billing, or compliance and therefore cannot safely use ordinary profile merge rules.
A concrete version-metadata design, including writer identity, metadata bounds, compaction, tombstone retention, and behavior after history loss.
Migration and mixed-version safeguards preventing legacy services, caches, APIs, or replicas from interpreting suspended accounts as active.
Failure-mode behavior for missing or corrupted causal history, metadata truncation, invalid reviewed-unsuspend signatures, and reconciliation-service outages.
Operational controls and validation metrics, including convergence monitoring, invariant checks, quarantine procedures, and alerts for attempted unsafe transitions.
Security requirements for authenticating and authorizing reviewed-unsuspend operations, including replay protection and approval provenance.
incorrect_assumptions: The assumption that writability applies only to profile updates is reasonable from evidence e5 but is not fully established by the broader statement that both systems can accept updates and the constraint that the system remain writable.
Treating 'suspended dominates active' as sufficient may be incorrect if there are additional account statuses or if an unsuspend must clear more than one independently issued suspension.
The report implicitly assumes bounded regional writers would make version-vector growth manageable, but the actual writer identity model is unknown.

It implicitly assumes deterministic per-field resolution always preserves acceptable user intent; some fields may require multi-value retention or manual review even if they are not authorization-sensitive.
critical_risks: An unsuspend rule that clears only one known suspension could reactivate an account while another concurrent or unseen suspension remains effective.
Mixed-version or legacy consumers could bypass the new merge policy and expose an active authorization state before reconciliation corrects it.
Loss, premature compaction, or corruption of causal metadata could make the system unable to prove that an unsuspend supersedes the relevant suspension.
Misclassifying an authorization-relevant profile field as ordinary could allow deterministic automatic merging to create a security regression.
Non-commutative or incompletely specified field rules could produce replica divergence despite operation deduplication.
recommended_changes: Lower confidence until the status state machine, writer topology, field classifications, and compatibility plan are confirmed.

Specify reviewed unsuspension formally: authentication requirements, causal preconditions, treatment of concurrent and later suspensions, replay behavior, and fail-closed handling when history is unavailable.
Select a concrete metadata scheme based on the number of replica and writer identities, then document ordering, concurrency detection, compaction, and recovery semantics.
Define and test a merge rule for every field and classify security-sensitive fields separately from ordinary profile data.
Add a migration protocol with version gating or fail-closed behavior so old consumers cannot process new status operations unsafely.
State explicitly that operation IDs provide identity and deduplication, while causal metadata provides ordering and concurrency detection.

Add property-based or model-based tests proving commutativity, associativity, idempotence, convergence, and the no-stale-reactivation invariant under duplicate, delayed, reordered, concurrent, and lost-history scenarios.
Add runtime invariant monitoring and quarantine any account whose status history cannot be safely reconciled.

strengths: The recommendation directly satisfies the three stated constraints: regional write availability, automatic profile convergence, and protection against stale status downgrades.
It correctly rejects wall-clock last-write-wins for authorization-sensitive status using the documented 47-second clock skew.
It treats reviewed unsuspension as a distinct authorized operation and identifies the crucial race between unsuspension and a concurrent or later suspension.
It appropriately calls for deterministic per-field policies, auditability, deduplication, and tests covering retries, duplicates, reordering, and hour-long partitions.
Its citations are traceable to the supplied evidence and generally support the associated claims.
weaknesses: The report recommends “version metadata” without selecting a concrete model or defining comparison, concurrency detection, metadata growth, and garbage-collection semantics.
The status merge rule is not specified as a complete state machine. “Causally supersede” does not define exactly which suspension a reviewed unsuspend authorizes or how concurrent operations resolve.

Profile reconciliation is left at the level of “per-field rules” and a “stable tie-breaker”; no rules are proposed for common cases such as deletion, null values, composite fields, or concurrent edits.
It does not define whether status and profile updates in one write must be reconciled atomically or may be split field-by-field.

The statement that unique operation IDs can support deterministic reconciliation is incomplete: IDs provide identity and deduplication, but deterministic convergence also requires identical merge inputs, rules, and ordering/tie-break semantics.
unsupported: The claim that rare profile conflicts support automatic deterministic reconciliation is not established by rarity; convergence depends on the merge algebra and implementation, not conflict frequency.
The report assumes unique operation IDs are suitable as reconciliation tie-breakers or ordering inputs, although the evidence establishes only uniqueness.
No evidence demonstrates that version metadata can be added compatibly or that all profile fields are authorization-neutral; the report correctly labels these as assumptions/evidence gaps.
missing: A formal status state machine covering active, suspended, reviewed unsuspend, repeated suspensions, duplicate operations, and concurrent suspension/unsuspension.
A rule binding each reviewed-unsuspend operation to the specific suspension or observed version it reviewed, preventing an old approval from clearing a newer suspension.
Explicit algebraic requirements for merge functions—determinism, commutativity, associativity, and idempotence—to guarantee convergence under reordering and duplication.
Authorization validation requirements for reviewed-unsuspend operations, including immutable actor, approval, scope, and integrity information.
Policies for profile-field deletion, schema evolution, unknown fields, malformed metadata, and records created independently in both regions.
Operational behavior when metadata is missing, corrupt, or from an older software version, plus rollout and backward-compatibility plans.
Verification that authorization reads cannot temporarily observe stale active status before reconciliation completes.
Monitoring, alerting, replay/rebuild procedures, retention limits, and a safe metadata-compaction strategy.
incorrect_assumptions: The wording may imply that causal ordering alone proves an unsuspend reviewed the relevant suspension. Causality only shows observation/order; the operation must explicitly reference or otherwise attest to the suspension/version reviewed.

The proposed safety rule assumes a “new suspension” can always be identified. Concurrent events are not intrinsically newer, so the policy must define suspension dominance unless the unsuspend explicitly covers that suspension.

If “monotonic status precedence” is interpreted as a permanently monotonic state value, legitimate reviewed unsuspension cannot be represented; monotonicity must apply to ordinary assignments while reviewed transitions use explicit semantics.
critical_risks: A reviewed-unsuspend operation replayed after a later suspension could reactivate a prohibited account unless it is scoped to a specific suspension/version.
Mixed software versions or divergent merge implementations across regions could produce non-convergent records or authorization regression.
Serving authorization decisions from unreconciled local state could allow access during a partition even if eventual reconciliation correctly restores suspension.
Metadata pruning without a proven causal-stability or tombstone strategy could resurrect stale active status or deleted profile values.
recommended_changes: Specify the account-status model formally: ordinary active writes never override suspension; suspension dominates concurrency; reviewed unsuspend must reference the suspension/version reviewed; any unreviewed or unobserved concurrent suspension dominates.

Choose and document a concrete causal metadata scheme, including event comparison, concurrent-event handling, deterministic tie-breakers, bounds, compaction, and migration behavior. Do not use wall-clock order for status safety.
Define merge rules for every profile field and verify that each rule is deterministic, commutative, associative, and idempotent.
Separate operation identity from ordering: use operation IDs for deduplication and only as a documented deterministic tie-breaker where business semantics permit.
Require cryptographically or otherwise integrity-protected authorization context for reviewed unsuspension and preserve it in immutable audit records.

Add safety tests for replayed old approvals, concurrent suspend/unsuspend, later suspension after review, mixed-version deployments, metadata loss, local authorization reads during partitions, and post-compaction reconciliation.
Clarify transactional semantics when one operation changes both profile and status fields, and define safe behavior for partial replication or application.

attacks: The recommendation may protect eventual reconciliation while failing the actual authorization invariant during a partition: a region that has not received a suspension can continue serving stale active status and authorizing access.
“Suspended dominates active” is not a complete rule. A reviewed unsuspend must identify every suspension it is authorized to clear; causal succession alone does not prove review scope.
The proposal conflates operation identity with ordering. Unique operation IDs enable deduplication but provide no causal order, semantic precedence, or convergence guarantee.
Conflict rarity is irrelevant to correctness. Even one authorization conflict is unacceptable, and automatic profile convergence depends on merge algebra rather than the 0.03% rate.
“Version metadata” conceals a major undecided design choice. Hybrid logical clocks, Lamport clocks, and version vectors provide materially different concurrency detection and compaction properties.
A field-specific merge can break record-level invariants when fields are correlated or when profile and status changes are intended to be atomic.
A stale reviewed-unsuspend operation can become a reusable reactivation capability unless bound to a specific suspension set/version and protected against replay.
Failing to classify profile fields could move the same security flaw into fields affecting roles, identity assurance, recovery channels, tenant membership, or risk controls.
Mixed-version replicas, caches, authorization services, and downstream consumers may bypass or misinterpret the new operation semantics.
Metadata pruning, tombstone loss, restore from backup, or partial history transfer can resurrect active state even when the normal merge function appears safe.
A deterministic tie-breaker can guarantee convergence while deterministically choosing the semantically wrong profile value; convergence is not correctness.
The asserted 0.98 recommendation confidence is unjustified before local authorization-read behavior, status-transition semantics, metadata feasibility, and migration safety are known.
falsifiers: During a partition, suspend an account in region A and issue authorization reads in disconnected region B; any successful authorization after the suspension falsifies the claimed safety outcome.
Generate concurrent suspensions S1 and S2, then replay an unsuspend approved only for S1; reactivation falsifies correct reviewed-unsuspend scoping.
Apply duplicate, reordered, and delayed operations in every permutation at both replicas; differing final records falsify deterministic convergence.
Replay an old reviewed-unsuspend after a later suspension; any transition to active falsifies stale-data safety.
Remove or compact causal metadata, restore one replica from an old backup, and reconcile; resurrection of active status falsifies recovery safety.
Run mixed old/new service versions against the same record; any consumer treating an unknown reviewed-unsuspend operation as ordinary active falsifies migration safety.
Execute an operation that atomically changes status and a correlated profile field, then partially replicate it; an invalid cross-field combination falsifies field-by-field merge safety.
Inventory authorization paths and profile fields; discovery of any automatically merged field that affects access control falsifies the authorization-neutral profile assumption.
Model-check the chosen merge functions for commutativity, associativity, and idempotence; any counterexample falsifies convergence under arbitrary delivery.
Issue an unsuspend with missing, forged, revoked, or mismatched approval context; acceptance falsifies the claimed controlled reactivation path.
Partition for longer than one hour or create an equivalent recovery backlog; unsafe behavior would falsify the assumption that one-hour testing bounds the relevant failure mode.
evidence_gaps: Whether the invariant prohibits only reconciliation-time downgrade or also any stale-active authorization decision before replicas reconnect.
A formal status state machine covering all statuses, repeated suspensions, concurrent operations, reviewed unsuspension, and replay.
The exact evidence a reviewed-unsuspend operation must carry and which suspension set or version it clears.
Whether status-changing operations remain writable in both regions during partitions and what local read semantics apply.
A complete classification of profile fields with authorization, authentication, fraud, billing, privacy, or compliance consequences.
A concrete metadata design with writer identities, comparison rules, concurrency detection, size bounds, compaction, tombstones, and disaster-recovery behavior.
Transactional requirements for writes spanning multiple profile fields or both profile and account status.
Proof that every merge rule is deterministic, commutative, associative, and idempotent across schema versions.
Compatibility behavior for legacy records, APIs, caches, replicas, event consumers, and authorization services.
Authorization and integrity controls for reviewed unsuspension, including approval provenance, scope, revocation, and replay prevention.
Evidence that authorization reads consume the safely merged state rather than stale caches or unreconciled regional records.
Operational controls for invariant monitoring, quarantine, metadata corruption, reconciliation outages, replay/rebuild, and unsafe-history recovery.
Maximum outage and recovery-backlog assumptions; the one-hour business requirement does not establish a technical upper bound.
Measurements of storage, latency, and migration impact from the proposed metadata and retained operation history.

accepted_criticisms: The report underspecified reviewed-unsuspend semantics: it must explicitly identify the suspension or observed suspension set/version it is authorized to clear; causal succession alone is insufficient.
Unique operation IDs provide identity and deduplication, not causal ordering, semantic precedence, or convergence by themselves.
Conflict rarity does not establish correctness or convergence; merge algebra and implementation do.
“Version metadata” leaves a material design decision unresolved, including concurrency detection, metadata bounds, compaction, recovery, and migration behavior.
Field-by-field reconciliation can violate cross-field invariants unless transactional groups and correlated fields are explicitly handled.
Reviewed-unsuspend operations need scope, integrity-protected approval context, revocation rules, and replay protection.
Every profile field must be classified because roles, tenant membership, recovery channels, identity assurance, and risk fields may affect authorization or security.
Mixed-version replicas, caches, authorization services, and downstream consumers require explicit compatibility and fail-safe behavior.
Metadata pruning, tombstone loss, partial history transfer, and backup restoration can resurrect stale state unless causal-stability and recovery rules are proven.
A deterministic tie-breaker guarantees convergence but not semantically correct profile values.
The original 0.98 confidence was too high given the unresolved state machine, local-read behavior, metadata scheme, field classification, and migration safety.
The status model needs formal rules for repeated and concurrent suspensions, duplicate operations, reviewed unsuspension, and stale approval replay.
Merge functions should be verified as deterministic, commutative, associative, and idempotent across supported schema versions.
rejected_criticisms: The claim that the recommendation necessarily violates the stated authorization invariant during a partition is not established. The visible constraint forbids stale data from downgrading suspended to active; it does not explicitly require disconnected regions to learn a remote suspension instantaneously, which is incompatible with unrestricted partition-time local authorization absent an external coordination mechanism.

The falsifier declaring any successful authorization in disconnected region B after a suspension in region A unsafe assumes a stronger global real-time revocation requirement than the problem states. It is a valuable requirement test, but not a valid falsifier until authorization-read semantics are clarified.

The recommendation should not be abandoned merely because conflicts are rare or because details remain open. Among the supplied options, field-specific merging is still the only option that can preserve required write availability while avoiding unsafe wall-clock status resolution.

Testing only partitions longer than one hour is not independently required by the supplied business constraint. Recovery backlogs and longer failures should be analyzed, but the stated one-hour requirement does not itself establish an unbounded availability obligation.
artifact.updated_recommendation: Retain the field-specific merge strategy, but make it conditional on a formal operation-based status model: suspension dominates ordinary active assignments and concurrent or unreviewed reactivation; a reviewed unsuspend must carry integrity-protected authorization context and explicitly cover the suspension set/version it clears; later or uncovered suspensions remain effective. Select a concrete causal metadata and compaction scheme, use operation IDs only for deduplication or documented tie-breaking, define invariant-preserving merge units and algebraic rules for every profile field, and require fail-safe migration, cache, authorization-read, replay, backup-restore, and mixed-version tests. If the intended invariant requires globally immediate suspension enforcement during partitions, none of the three options as stated is sufficient; authorization would need coordination, fail-closed reads, or a separate globally available revocation mechanism.
reasons: Wall-clock last-write-wins remains unsafe given observed 47-second clock skew.
Disabling regional writes conflicts with the explicit partition-time profile-write requirement.
Field-specific reconciliation remains the best supplied option, but the original report described a direction rather than a complete safety protocol.
The strongest criticisms identify genuine missing specifications and verification obligations without disproving the option-level recommendation.
The local authorization-read criticism exposes an ambiguity in the required invariant, so the recommendation must explicitly branch on whether safety is reconciliation-time or globally immediate.
Confidence is reduced because feasibility and correctness depend on unresolved metadata, state-machine, migration, recovery, and field-classification evidence.

accepted_criticisms: The reviewed-unsuspend semantics are underspecified: causal succession alone does not establish which concurrent or repeated suspensions an approval may clear.
Unique operation IDs provide identity and deduplication, not causal ordering, semantic precedence, or convergence.
Conflict rarity does not establish correctness; automatic convergence requires properly defined merge algebra.
The metadata choice is materially unresolved because version vectors, Lamport clocks, and hybrid logical clocks have different concurrency, growth, compaction, and recovery properties.
Field-by-field merging can violate cross-field atomicity or record-level invariants, and security-relevant profile fields require stricter classification.
Reviewed unsuspend must be authenticated, scoped to a specific suspension set or causal frontier, and protected against stale replay.
Mixed-version replicas, caches, authorization services, and downstream consumers require fail-closed migration behavior.
Metadata loss, compaction, backup restoration, and partial history transfer can resurrect unsafe state unless recovery semantics are explicitly designed.
Deterministic tie-breaking guarantees convergence, not semantic correctness.
The original 0.98 confidence was too high given the missing state machine, metadata design, field classification, authorization-read semantics, and migration plan.
The report should explicitly distinguish reconciliation safety from partition-time authorization safety; a disconnected region may still authorize from stale active state.
Testing only partitions of at least one hour does not cover longer outages, recovery backlogs, compaction, or history-loss scenarios.
Auditability requires durable history, actor and approval provenance, logical ordering, and retention controls—not operation IDs alone.
rejected_criticisms: The criticisms do not justify switching to wall-clock last-write-wins: the documented 47-second clock skew makes it unsafe for authorization-sensitive status.
The criticisms do not justify disabling all writes in one region: that conflicts with the stated requirement that both regions accept profile updates during partitions.

The claim that partition-time stale authorization necessarily falsifies the stated reconciliation strategy is too broad unless the invariant is confirmed to govern authorization decisions before replication; it is nevertheless a critical evidence gap requiring a fail-closed authorization design.
The report did not claim that the 0.03% conflict rate proves correctness; it used rarity only as context for preserving availability, although the phrasing should not be treated as safety evidence.
artifact.updated_recommendation: Still choose field-specific merge rules with monotonic status precedence and causal version metadata, but treat this as a conditional architecture decision rather than an implementation-ready design. Formally require that active authorization is permitted only when a valid, authenticated, non-replayed reviewed-unsuspend explicitly observes and clears every applicable suspension; concurrent, later, unknown, or history-unverifiable suspensions must keep the account suspended. Classify all security-sensitive and correlated fields, define associative, commutative, and idempotent merge rules or atomic operation boundaries, select a concrete bounded metadata and recovery scheme, and gate mixed-version consumers fail-closed. Separately define partition-time authorization behavior so a region with stale active state cannot continue granting access after an unseen suspension if the invariant applies before reconciliation.
reasons: The original option remains the only listed strategy capable of combining automatic profile convergence, partition-time profile writability, and protection from stale status overwrite.
The supplied evidence directly rules against wall-clock last-write-wins and supports a distinct reviewed-unsuspend operation.
The core recommendation was correct at the option-selection level, so no position change is warranted.

Confidence must fall because the visible evidence does not establish a complete status state machine, unsuspend scope, local authorization behavior, metadata feasibility, cross-field invariants, recovery safety, or migration compatibility.
Implementation acceptance should depend on model checking and adversarial tests covering duplicate, reordered, concurrent, replayed, compacted, restored, and mixed-version histories.

artifact.decision: Choose field-specific merge rules with monotonic status precedence and causal version metadata, conditionally; this is the best supplied option but not yet an implementation-ready safety design.
artifact.action: Approve the option-level direction subject to a formal status state machine, scoped and replay-safe reviewed-unsuspend operations, concrete causal metadata and recovery semantics, field classification, fail-closed compatibility behavior, and adversarial convergence and authorization testing. If the invariant requires immediate cross-region revocation during partitions, reject all three options and add coordination, fail-closed authorization reads, or a separate globally available revocation mechanism.
reasons: Wall-clock last-write-wins is unsafe for authorization-sensitive status because observed clock skew can misorder stale active and suspension operations.
Disabling one region's writes conflicts with the explicit requirement that both regions accept profile updates during partitions lasting up to one hour.
Field-specific reconciliation is the only listed option capable of combining partition-time profile writability, automatic profile convergence, and protection against stale status overwrite.
Suspended-over-active precedence is necessary but insufficient: reviewed unsuspension must explicitly cover every applicable suspension and must resist replay.
Unique operation IDs support identity and deduplication, but causal ordering, semantic precedence, and convergence require additional metadata and merge algebra.
The visible evidence supports selecting an architectural direction but does not establish metadata feasibility, migration safety, recovery safety, or partition-time authorization behavior.
evidence: Evidence e1 states that regional clock skew has reached 47 seconds, directly undermining wall-clock ordering for status safety.
Evidence e3 defines the required semantic precedence: suspended dominates active until an explicit reviewed unsuspend.
Evidence e5 requires both regions to continue accepting profile updates during partitions up to one hour, ruling out blanket single-region writability.
Evidence e6 confirms that reconciliation code can distinguish reviewed-unsuspend operations from ordinary updates, enabling distinct transition semantics.
Evidence e4 confirms unique operation IDs are already attached to writes, supporting deduplication but not ordering.

The reviews and rebuttals consistently identify unresolved status-transition, metadata, replay, mixed-version, field-classification, and recovery requirements; these are supported by the absence of such specifications in the problem artifact.
rejected_alternatives: Reject wall-clock last-write-wins for every field because the documented clock skew can let stale active data defeat a suspension.
Reject disabling writes in one region whenever connectivity is uncertain because it violates required partition-time profile writability.
Reject unconditional approval of the field-specific strategy because the visible artifacts do not define a complete safety protocol.
Reject permanent suspended-dominates-active semantics without a scoped reviewed transition because it could prevent legitimate reactivation.
Reject operation IDs as a substitute for causal metadata or merge algebra; uniqueness alone provides neither ordering nor convergence.
Reject conflict rarity as evidence of correctness; frequency does not prove merge safety.
minority: A stronger interpretation of the invariant may require that no disconnected region authorize an account after another region suspends it. Under that interpretation, none of the three listed options is sufficient.

A narrower interpretation only prohibits stale active data from winning during reconciliation. Under that interpretation, the selected option can satisfy the stated invariant once its transition and merge semantics are completed.
unresolved: Whether the safety invariant applies only to reconciliation outcomes or also to every partition-time authorization decision.

citation_checks.note: The artifact explicitly states that clock skew between regions reached 47 seconds. This supports rejecting wall-clock last-write-wins for safety-sensitive status.
The 0.03 percent conflict rate is present, but the added claim that rarity supports deterministic reconciliation is not established; convergence depends on merge algebra.
